items.resolution: The writeback gives probe results to an admission path rather than treating them as a correctness proof, separates the probe and symbolic-execution responsibilities, and keeps unsupported kernels on a conservative fallback. The empirical and completeness limits match exact-v1 Sections 4 through 6.

The chapter describes an optional signed, self-reported completion block. It distinguishes attribution and tamper evidence from independent effect proof, avoids inventing a failure receipt, and preserves counter-signing, third-party attestation and external effect verification as stronger paths.

Passed after correction: exact-v1 Sections 4.1 through 4.4 define the same-model block-size-one verifier, self-verification mode, routing policies and analysis, while Section 5 carries the experiments. The Daily, queue and Books boundary now preserve authoritative verification and commit semantics, bind gains to router and acceptance behavior, and retain direct decoding as fallback.
